answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 68% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the kernel registry records each claim and the sonnet audit publishes every slash. A farm must as a result either lie, which the terrace graph proves on replay, or recruit 141 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 27 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
